summary:
Found and fixed the needle. ✅

## The bug
`computeHandler` in `main.go` spawned a background goroutine running `performComputation`, but that computation had no way to be cancelled. When a client disconnected (or the request timed out), the handler returned — but the goroutine kept spinning through its full iteration/sleep loop, leaking one goroutine per abandoned request.

## The fix
- Derived a cancellable context from `r.Context()` (which Go cancels automatically on client disconnect), with a 25s overall timeout.
- Threaded that context into `performComputation`, which now checks `ctx.Err()` each iteration and uses a `select` on `ctx.Done()` instead of a blocking `time.Sleep`, returning early when cancelled.
- Made the goroutine send its result via a non-blocking `select` so it can't block on the buffered channel after the handler has gone away.

Test result: goroutines stay at baseline (4) after 20 client disconnects — **0 leaked**. All tests pass.
